allOf.description: Inherits shared step-base properties ($schema, id, owner, created_at, canonical_refs_used).

ambiguities.description: Open ambiguities this step could not settle; each names what it is about. An item is deleted once its answer is applied.

environments.description: Map of environment names to environment nodes. Each key must be one of the canonical environment names (dev, ci, staging, prod) and all four are required. Each value is an environment node (scope, derives_from, ...) whose optional config object is a key-value map capturing environment-specific overrides for infrastructure, scaling, and feature flags. Decision rule: put in config only keys whose value differs across at least two environments — if a key has the same value in every environment, omit it; shared defaults belong in application configuration, not here. Correct: {"dev": {"scope": "in", "derives_from": ["seed-delivery"], "config": {"replica_count": 1, "log_level": "debug"}}}. Anti-pattern: a host key at the environment level (it must sit under config); duplicating keys with identical values across all environments, which creates a false impression that values vary.

propertyNames.description: Environment name constraint: must be a valid environment (dev, ci, staging, prod).

additionalProperties.description: One deployment environment: node fields (scope, derives_from, ...) plus an optional config object holding the settings that differ between tiers — e.g., replica count, database URL pattern, feature flags, resource limits. Values should reflect actual delivery targets, not placeholder strings.

config.description: Host configuration for this environment: the key-value settings that differ between tiers. Optional; every host key lives here, never beside the node fields. When present it holds at least one key, and each key is lowercase (letters, digits, '-' and '_', starting with a letter).

scope.description: Delivery scope for this environment: 'in' for the current release, 'later' for deferred work, 'out' for explicitly excluded work. 'later' and 'out' require scope_reason.

scope_reason.description: Why this environment is later or out of scope. Required when scope is later or out.

derives_from.description: Ids of the seeds, constraints or scope items this environment is derived from. At least one is required; every environment must be justified by what it derives from.

assumes.description: Ids of the charter assumptions this environment relies on. Optional; omit when it rests on no recorded assumption.

lifecycle.description: Lifecycle state of this environment: active (default), deprecated or not_applicable.

aliases.description: Former names of this environment. An environment is a map-keyed node: `specdev node rename` does not rename it, so these names are written by hand. Optional.

replaces.description: Ids of nodes that this environment replaces. Optional.

ci_gates.description: Ordered list of CI gates that must all pass before a deployment is considered promotable. At least one gate must be provided (enforced by minItems). Decision rule: the name must be recognizable to a developer reading the CI log — use kebab-case that matches what the gate actually validates. Standard names: 'unit-tests', 'lint', 'type-check', 'security-scan', 'integration-tests', 'e2e-smoke', 'coverage-check'. Worked examples (gate_id values): unit-tests, lint, type-check, security-scan for a typical backend service; unit-tests, integration-tests, e2e-smoke, coverage-check for a full-stack app. Anti-pattern: 'tests' (ambiguous — unit, integration, or e2e?), 'CI' (too generic to be actionable), 'checks' (not machine-identifiable); also avoid capital letters and spaces as they break pipeline job name matching.

items.description: A single CI gate that must pass before a deployment is promotable, with its scope and the components or constraints it derives from.

gate_id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier of this CI gate (e.g., 'unit-tests', 'lint', 'security-scan'). Should match a pipeline job name in the host repo's CI configuration.

scope.description: Delivery scope for this CI gate: 'in' for the current release, 'later' for deferred work, 'out' for explicitly excluded work. 'later' and 'out' require scope_reason.

scope_reason.description: Why this CI gate is later or out of scope. Required when scope is later or out.

derives_from.description: Ids of the components or constraints this CI gate is derived from. At least one is required; every CI gate must be justified by what it derives from. A seed routed to this step may be listed in addition, for content taken straight from the seed and not through an upstream node; a seed alone does not satisfy the field.

assumes.description: Ids of the charter assumptions this CI gate relies on. Optional; omit when it rests on no recorded assumption.

lifecycle.description: Lifecycle state of this CI gate: active (default), deprecated or not_applicable.

aliases.description: Former ids of this CI gate; `specdev node rename` adds the old id here. Optional.

replaces.description: Ids of nodes that this CI gate replaces. Optional.

secrets.description: List of secrets (environment variable keys) that the delivery pipeline requires at runtime. Each entry is a secret node whose name is the exact env-var name injected by the secrets manager. This list drives audit trails and helps reviewers confirm all secrets are provisioned before deployment. Omit internal framework secrets that are auto-injected by the platform.

items.description: A single secret the delivery pipeline requires, with its env-var name, scope and the nodes it derives from.

secret_id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier of this secret node (e.g., 'secret-database-url'). Minted; the env-var name itself is the name field.

name.description: Exact env-var name injected by the secrets manager — e.g., 'DATABASE_URL', 'API_KEY_STRIPE', 'JWT_SECRET'. Do not include values or partial keys.

scope.description: Delivery scope for this secret: 'in' for the current release, 'later' for deferred work, 'out' for explicitly excluded work. 'later' and 'out' require scope_reason.

scope_reason.description: Why this secret is later or out of scope. Required when scope is later or out.

derives_from.description: Ids of the connections, components or constraints this secret is derived from. At least one is required; every secret must be justified by what it derives from. A seed routed to this step may be listed in addition, for content taken straight from the seed and not through an upstream node; a seed alone does not satisfy the field.

assumes.description: Ids of the charter assumptions this secret relies on. Optional; omit when it rests on no recorded assumption.

lifecycle.description: Lifecycle state of this secret: active (default), deprecated or not_applicable.

aliases.description: Former ids of this secret; `specdev node rename` adds the old id here. Optional.

replaces.description: Ids of nodes that this secret replaces. Optional.

compliance.description: The compliance regimes this delivery baseline declares: the compliance standards or regulatory frameworks it must satisfy. Use canonical short names: 'SOC2', 'GDPR', 'HIPAA', 'PCI-DSS', 'ISO27001'. Each entry should reflect an actual external or internal obligation — not aspirational standards. If no formal compliance applies, use an empty array rather than inventing entries.

environment_ref.description: Canonical reference to the environment definitions in the canonical registry. Kind must be 'environment'. Example: {"id": "cn:core:environment:prod", "kind": "environment", "label": "prod"}. Common IDs: 'cn:core:environment:prod', 'cn:core:environment:staging', 'cn:core:environment:dev'. Should match one of the keys in the 'environments' object of this artifact. Validated by canonical-integrity lint.

command_ref.description: Canonical reference to the CLI command this CI gate invokes. Kind is structurally pinned to 'command'. Example: {"id": "cn:core:command:pytest", "kind": "command"} for pytest. Only reference commands registered in the canon.

policy_ref.description: Canonical reference to the governance policy this baseline configuration enforces. Kind is structurally pinned to 'policy'. Example: {"id": "cn:core:policy:spec-first", "kind": "policy"}. Validated by canonical-integrity lint.
